name: SketchForge-3D
description: A local-first browser 3D design editor for building, cutting, importing STL files, and exporting models.
readme_summary: SketchForge-3D is a local-first, browser-based 3D design editor that allows users to build, modify, import, and export 3D models directly in their web browser. It focuses on a streamlined workflow for creating parts without requiring accounts or heavy software installations.
key_features: Local-first projects stored in browser storage
Real 3D workplane with camera and snap controls
Primitive shape library (boxes, cylinders, spheres, etc.)
Solid and hole workflow for boolean operations
Boolean Intersection
Reversible edge tools (chamfer, fillet)
STL import
STL, OBJ, and STEP export
Fast browser stack (Next.js, React, TypeScript, Three.js)
primary_use_case: Quickly designing and exporting 3D models for various purposes, such as 3D printing or prototyping, directly within a web browser without complex setup.
cover_image_prompt: A skilled artisan in a bright, airy workshop, using a magical, glowing chisel to precisely carve intricate details into a block of digital clay. The clay block is clearly composed of basic geometric shapes like cubes and spheres, some of which are being 'cut out' to form holes. On a nearby workbench, a tablet displays the SketchForge-3D interface, showing the same model being manipulated. Small, stylized STL files float gently in the background, representing imported and exported models. The overall mood is one of effortless creation and precision. The art style should be a clean, 3D isometric illustration with a focus on clear forms and a bright, inviting color palette, subtly incorporating the SketchForge-3D logo on the artisan's apron.

name: pgrok
description: Personal ngrok alternative. Expose local ports to the internet with automatic HTTPS via SSH tunnels + Caddy.
readme_summary: pgrok is a personal alternative to ngrok that exposes local ports to the internet using SSH tunnels and Caddy for automatic HTTPS. It features an interactive TUI dashboard for monitoring and debugging.
key_features: Expose local ports to the internet
Automatic HTTPS via Caddy
SSH reverse tunnels
Interactive TUI dashboard
HTTP request inspection
On-demand TLS certificate provisioning
primary_use_case: Exposing local development servers or applications to the internet for testing, collaboration, or public access, with the added benefit of secure HTTPS connections and real-time monitoring.
cover_image_prompt: A stylized, magical bridge extending from a local computer screen, across a digital void, to a vibrant, bustling city representing the internet. The bridge is formed by glowing SSH tunnel lines, and at the city's entrance, a friendly robot (representing Caddy) is handing out secure HTTPS certificates. Small, colorful icons representing web requests flow across the bridge. The pgrok logo is subtly integrated into the bridge's structure. The overall mood is one of seamless connection and secure access, rendered in a clean, modern 3D isometric illustration style with a bright, inviting color palette.

name: ProxyBridge
description: Proxifier Alternative to redirect any Windows/MacOS/Linux TCP and UDP traffic to HTTP/Socks5 proxy
readme_summary: ProxyBridge is a universal proxy client for Windows, macOS, and Linux that acts as a Proxifier alternative. It enables transparent redirection of TCP and UDP traffic from applications through SOCKS5 or HTTP proxies, allowing granular control over traffic routing, blocking, or allowing on a per-application basis.
key_features: Universal proxy client for Windows, macOS, and Linux
Transparent proxy routing for TCP and UDP traffic
Supports SOCKS5 and HTTP proxies
Per-application traffic control (route, block, allow)
Works at the system level, compatible with proxy-unaware applications
primary_use_case: To provide transparent system-wide proxying for TCP and UDP traffic on Windows, macOS, and Linux, allowing users to route traffic through SOCKS5 or HTTP proxies on a per-application basis.
cover_image_prompt: A stylized, friendly robot acting as a traffic controller at a busy intersection. Instead of cars, streams of digital data (glowing blue and green lines) are flowing towards the intersection. The robot is directing these data streams, with some lines being rerouted through a large, stylized 'SOCKS5/HTTP Proxy' tunnel, while others are explicitly blocked by red 'X' signs or allowed through green 'checkmarks'. Small, subtle UI elements resembling application icons are visible near the data streams, indicating which application's traffic is being controlled. The background is a clean, abstract digital landscape. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a bright, clear color palette, emphasizing control and redirection.

name: textual-web
description: Run TUIs and terminals in your browser
readme_summary: Textual Web allows users to run Textual applications and terminals directly in their web browser. It acts as a bridge, making TUIs accessible remotely and shareable via public URLs, simplifying the deployment and access of terminal-based applications.
key_features: Publish Textual apps and terminals on the web
Run TUIs in a browser
Generate public URLs for apps and terminals
Serve multiple apps and terminals via configuration
Support for serving raw terminals with optional commands
primary_use_case: To make Textual-based terminal applications and raw terminals accessible and shareable through a web browser interface.
cover_image_prompt: A vibrant, stylized illustration of a web browser window acting as a portal. Inside the portal, a complex, glowing Textual application interface is clearly visible and interactive. Emerging from the browser portal are several distinct streams of light, each leading to a different, simplified icon representing a terminal or a specific application. The background is a subtle, abstract representation of the internet, with faint network lines. The repository name 'textual-web' is subtly integrated into the browser's UI or as a small watermark. The overall mood is modern, accessible, and slightly magical, emphasizing the transformation of terminal interfaces into web-friendly experiences. 3D isometric illustration style with clean lines and a bright color palette.

name: swarms
description: The Enterprise-Grade Multi-Agent Orchestration Framework. Website: https://swarms.ai
readme_summary: Swarms is an enterprise-grade, production-ready framework for orchestrating multi-agent systems. It provides scalable and adaptive architectures for sequential, concurrent, and hierarchical agent interactions, with backward compatibility and interoperability with various AI protocols.
key_features: Enterprise-grade multi-agent orchestration
Production-ready architectures (sequential, concurrent, hierarchical)
Scalable and adaptive systems
Backward compatibility with leading agent frameworks
Interoperability with protocols like MCP, x402, skills
Agent definition: LLM + Tools + Memory
primary_use_case: Orchestrating complex multi-agent AI systems in production environments.
cover_image_prompt: A conductor leading a symphony orchestra, where each musician is an AI agent represented by a distinct, glowing orb. The conductor, holding a digital baton, seamlessly directs the flow of information (visualized as streams of light) between the agents, creating a harmonious and complex output on a large, central screen displaying a sophisticated AI-generated artwork. Subtle UI elements showing agent status and communication protocols are integrated into the conductor's podium. The scene is set in a futuristic, minimalist concert hall with dramatic lighting, emphasizing collaboration and intelligent direction. The style is a 3D isometric illustration with vibrant, glowing elements and clean lines.

name: imgcompress
description: Imgcompress is a self-hosted image processing toolbox that handles compression, format conversion, and AI background removal in a single web interface. It supports over 70 input formats (including PSD, HEIC, and RAW) and can output common formats or generate PDFs, all without sending files to external services.
readme_summary: ImgCompress is a self-hosted, Docker-based image processing toolbox that offers a comprehensive suite of tools for compression, format conversion, and AI-powered background removal. It operates entirely locally, ensuring user privacy and data security by processing all files within the user's own container without external uploads.
key_features: Support for over 70 image formats (including PSD, HEIC, RAW, EPS, TIFF, WebP)
Local AI background removal (no API keys or uploads required)
Bulk image compression with multi-core parallel processing
Format conversion capabilities (e.g., HEIC to WebP, PSD to JPG, batches to PDF)
Per-file cropping with various aspect ratio presets and custom dimensions
Web UI and CLI for flexible usage
Single Docker container deployment with zero host dependencies
Offline and air-gap ready operation
primary_use_case: To provide a private, self-hosted solution for batch image processing, including compression, format conversion, and AI background removal, for users who want to maintain full control over their data and avoid cloud-based services.
cover_image_prompt: A digital alchemist in a dimly lit, private workshop, meticulously transforming raw, unrefined ore (representing various image formats like PSD, HEIC, RAW) into polished, perfectly shaped gemstones (representing compressed, converted, and background-removed images). The alchemist uses a glowing, intricate workbench with subtle UI elements displaying format types and compression levels. Digital particles representing data flow from the raw materials to the finished gems. The repository name 'ImgCompress' is subtly etched onto a tool. The scene is rendered in a 3D isometric illustration style with a focus on detail and a rich, warm color palette, emphasizing the transformation and local processing.
